setup.title: Welcome to FE Maker
setup.intro: Choose your copy of Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones (US version). It stays on your computer.
setup.invalid: This file is not Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones (US). Make sure you have the right, unmodified version.
home.name: Game name
home.author: Author
ws.startHint: Test builds only. "Straight onto the map" creates a game (normal mode, no tutorial) and starts the first chapter; press Start to skip the opening event. The exported patch always keeps the normal start of the game.
field.name: Name
field.averageHint: What the character will have on average, from their growth rates. With a promotion the level goes back to 1: the second level counts in the new class. Promotion gains and each class's limits are taken into account.
character.colors.title: Colours in battle
character.colors.portraitHint: Tries the portrait's colours on this class, on the side shown: hair, clothes and a wyvern's body. The horse, the pegasus's wings and the weapon stay. Nothing is replaced until you keep the result; you can touch it up by clicking on the sprite.
character.colors.swapHint: Drag a colour onto another to swap them, for instance if the hair and the clothes came out the wrong way round. Drag the handle on the left of a group onto another group to swap all their shades.
character.colors.clickSprite: Click a part of the character to recolour it.
character.colors.family: New colour for this part ({n} shades)
character.colors.hint: This character's colours in their battle animation, class by class and by side. Click the sprite to recolour a part with its shades, or change the squares one by one: hover one to see what it colours.
field.basesHint: These values are added to the class bases.
field.classHint: The class applies wherever the character appears: the character sheet is the only source of its class. Watch out for weapons reserved for the previous class (see the item editor). Level and inventory are set chapter by chapter.
field.noAnimation: This class has no battle animation for this weapon type
field.noAnimationHint: ⚠ = the class has no battle animation for this weapon type: a rank in it would crash the game.
field.inventoryLater: Starting inventory depends on the chapter: it will be editable with chapters (phase 3).
field.lockedToNobody: nobody (no class or character has this lock)
build.launched: The game is starting in mGBA.
build.firstTime: The first build takes about ten minutes, the next ones a few seconds.
keys.title: Controls
keys.intro: Click a button, then press the key you want (Esc to cancel).
keys.saved: Controls saved. They will apply on the next "Test".
keys.duplicate: The same key is used for two buttons.
field.affinityHint: Affinity works through supports: when two linked characters are in range (3 tiles), each gains the bonuses of their own affinity and of the other's, per support rank (C = 1, B = 2, A = 3).
field.convoyAccessHint: This character, and the units next to them, get the "Supply" command. In the game: Eirika and Ephraim (the lord of the chosen route).
chapter.convoyHint: On by default in a blank project and in added chapters. In the game there is none in the prologue, chapters 1 and 5x and Castle Frelia.
portrait.title: Replace with a picture
portrait.shared: The same pictures are also used by portraits #{ids}.
portrait.hint: 128 × 112 sheet, 16 colors (the top left corner is transparent). Download the current sheet for a template.
portrait.missing: Portrait #{id} does not exist (any more): choose another portrait number.
portrait.name: Name
portrait.addedHint: Portrait added by the project, after the game's ones. Dialogues can show it like the others.
portrait.deleteHint: Characters and dialogues using it will need another one.
portrait.newHint: Adds a portrait without replacing this one.
problem.portrait.noFreePortrait: no free portrait number left (254 at most)
ferepo.hint: Community resources. Authors go to CREDITS.txt by themselves. F2E: free to use and edit; F2U: free to use only.
ferepo.notSheet: This file is not a 128 × 112 portrait sheet (parts, tutorial…): it cannot be imported as it is.
ferepo.license.F2E: F2E: free to use and edit (crediting the authors)
ferepo.license.F2U: F2U: free to use (crediting the authors), but not to edit without their consent
ferepo.error.unreachable: FE-Repo cannot be reached (no internet connection?)
ferepo.error.notFeRepo: this file is not from FE-Repo
ferepo.error.notAnImage: this file is not a PNG picture
problem.portrait.unreachable: FE-Repo cannot be reached (no internet connection?)
problem.portrait.notFeRepo: this file is not from FE-Repo
problem.portrait.tooManyColors: the sheet has more than 16 colors
problem.portrait.notAnImage: this file is not a readable PNG picture
problem.portrait.cut: part of the picture falls outside what the game shows (top corners of the face, top-right corner)
ability.title: Abilities
ability.hint: They add to the class abilities (greyed boxes). A weapon lock gives access to the reserved weapons shown in brackets.
ability.mountedAid: Aid computed as a mounted unit
ability.bit23: Replaced by the previous character of the list
ability.negateLethality: Immune to lethality, gives no experience
class.genericPortraitHint: The class card or portrait of units whose character has none, like nameless soldiers. A character with a portrait of their own keeps it.
class.statsHint: Base: added to the stats of every character of the class. Automatic level growth: only for units given automatic levels, mostly enemies; a played unit grows with its character's growths, never with these. Luck has no class base or maximum (fixed cap of 30).
class.weaponRanksHint: A rank in a weapon type allows wielding it. ⚠ = no battle animation for that type: the game would crash.
combat.triangleHint: When the attacker uses the first type against the second, it gets these bonuses (and the defender the same as penalties).
combat.effectivenessHint: A weapon effective against a list triples its might against the classes in it (only x2 for 8 legendary weapons, an engine rule). Each weapon picks its list in the Items tab.
reserve.title: Reserved weapon
reserve.toggle: Reserved for some characters or classes
reserve.hint: Only the listed characters and classes can wield it (they also need the weapon rank). FE Maker manages the engine's weapon locks itself: at most 6 different lists.
field.monsterWeaponHint: Special engine behavior: no rank needed, unbreakable, reserved for classes with the "Monster weapons" talent.
ability.desc.boss: +40 EXP when defeated, boss icon on the map, resists lethality (25% instead of 50%)
ability.desc.promoted: Already promoted class: cannot promote again
ability.desc.supply: Left over from FE7 (Merlinus): cannot trade or be rescued, comes back after death. Does not open the convoy by itself: also tick "Opens the convoy".
ability.desc.thiefSkills: Opens chests and doors without keys
ability.desc.dance: Dances to let a unit act again
ability.desc.play: Plays music to let a unit act again
ability.desc.lethality: Chance to kill an enemy in one blow (lethality)
ability.desc.mountedAid: Aid (carrying units) computed as a mounted unit
ability.desc.unselectable: The player cannot select the unit
ability.desc.negateLethality: Cannot be killed in one blow
ability.desc.bit23: Engine flag with no known effect
chapter.sideHint: To recruit an allied unit: a "Talk" dialogue in Dialogues, with "recruits".
chapter.levelBonusHint: The game takes these levels from enemies in Easy and Normal and adds them in Hard, with the stats that go with them. This applies to all enemies, bosses included, with automatic levels or not. Only playable characters placed on the enemy side do not get it.
chapter.allyItemsHint: If this character is already in the army, they keep their items, level and class: only the position counts. These items are only used on their first appearance.
chapter.pickUnit: Click a unit on the map to see its sheet.
chapter.editHint: Click a group to see its units, a unit to change it; drag it on the map to move it.
chapter.autolevelHint: The game levels the unit up to this level and gives it the stats that go with it. Without this box it shows the level but keeps its starting stats. A named ally starts from the level on their sheet with their own growths; an enemy or a generic follows its class.
chapter.fixedPath: This unit enters by a fixed path: it cannot be moved here.
problem.nameTooLong: names longer than {max} characters may overflow
problem.noBattleAnimation: the class has no battle animation for this weapon type: the game may crash
problem.unusedClass: class never used in the original game: its sprites or animations may be incomplete
problem.tooManyReservations: at most {max} different "reserved for" lists (engine limit)
chapter.addUnit: Add a unit to this group (copy of the last one)
chapter.copyHint: An added unit keeps the AI and other settings of the unit it copies, without its entry path.
chapter.removeHint: Careful: the chapter's events may refer to this character (dialogues, victory conditions).
problem.noCharacter: no character: this unit and the next ones in the group would vanish
problem.sameTile: another unit of the group starts on the same tile ({x}, {y})
problem.tooManyUnits: at most {max} units of this side in a group (engine limit)
ai.action.10: Only targets a unit set by the game
ai.action.12: Attacks if the enemy is very close
ai.action.14: Heals allies at 50% HP or less
ai.action.15: Alternates healing and attacking in place
ai.action.17: Waits until a door is opened
ai.move.4: Loots villages and chests, then moves towards the enemy
ai.move.5: Loots villages and chests, then flees
ai.move.6: Moves when an enemy is 2 turns away
ai.move.7: Moves when an enemy is 2 turns away (game exception)
ai.move.10: Moves towards a target set by the game
ai.move.11: Moves towards a target set by the game (variant)
ai.move.15: Moves towards the enemy even behind a wall
ai.move.16: Guards an area set by the game
ai.move.17: Waits one turn, loots, then moves
ai.move.18: Waits one turn, then moves towards the enemy
ai.preset.inRange: Attacks if an enemy is in range, otherwise waits
ai.preset.standGround: Stays put, attacks from its tile
ai.preset.approach: Waits for an enemy to come close, then chases
ai.title: Behavior (AI)
ai.playerHint: The player controls these units: the AI only matters if the unit changes sides.
problem.badAi: AI value outside the engine tables
ticket.buttonTitle: Report a bug or suggest an idea
ticket.title: Tickets
ticket.kind.question: Question
ticket.placeholder: What happened, what you expected, how to reproduce it…
ticket.pasteHint: Paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V. Ctrl+Enter to send.
ticket.showClosed: Also show done or dropped tickets
ticket.error.imageTooBig: Image too large (8 MB at most).
ws.simplePrologueHint: For tests: the prologue starts without its cutscene or units walking in; they are already in place. Does not affect the exported patch.
chapter.showGroup: Show this group on the map
chapter.openGroup: Open the group: list of its units
combat.triangleVisualHint: Each arrow goes from the type with the advantage to the one at a disadvantage. Values are the bonus of the winner; the other gets the opposite.
chapter.cutsceneHint: These units only appear in an event played before the battle, often on another map. Editing them does not change the battle. Tick a group to see it on the map.
chapter.cutsceneUnit: Cutscene unit: changing it does not change the battle.
chapter.goToBattleUnit: See this character in the battle →
objective.title: Objective
objective.hint.seize: The lord wins by choosing "Seize" on the tile (throne, gate…).
objective.hint.defeat_all: The chapter is won when no enemy is left.
objective.hint.defeat_boss: The chapter is won when the boss chosen below is defeated (or when no enemy is left).
objective.hint.defense: The chapter is won at the start of the turn after the last turn to hold.
objective.hint.special: Special objective of the original game.
objective.picking: Click a tile on the map…
objective.label: Goal window:
objective.orBossHint: Also won if the boss is defeated before the turns run out.
objective.statusShared: This text is shared with {n} other chapter(s): editing it changes them too.
objective.eventsShared: This chapter's events are shared with {n} other chapter(s): changing the objective changes them too.
objective.readOnly.custom: This objective is written in a special way in the original game (areas, combined conditions…): FE Maker cannot edit it yet. The text can still be edited.
objective.readOnly.noEvents: This chapter has no events: no objective to edit.
problem.objectiveTextTooLong: at most {lines} lines of {max} characters, or the text may overflow
chapter.classFromSheet: Class set on the sheet of
chapter.levelFromSheet: Level set on the sheet of
list.unusedClasses: Classes never used in the game ({n})
field.lastWordsHint: What this character says when they fall. Opens their line in the dialogues, created if they have none yet.
ticket.replyPlaceholder: What you want to add… Ctrl+V to paste a screenshot.
objective.noBoss: No boss: the chapter will only be won by defeating all enemies.
objective.bossAbsent: This character is not among the chapter's battle units: add it, or it cannot be defeated.
objective.bossAbility: Tip: give them the "Boss" ability on their sheet.
objective.bossQuote: The original boss's last words are not kept for the new boss.
objective.bossPerRoute: This chapter has a different boss on each route: not editable yet.
maps.shared: editing this map changes all {n} chapters
maps.hint: Pick a tile and paint. Its terrain comes with it.
maps.changed: {n} cell(s) changed from the original game.
maps.tool.penHint: Paints the cells under the mouse (hold the button to draw).
maps.tool.rectHint: Click and drag to fill a rectangle.
maps.tool.fillHint: Replaces the whole area of the same tile around the clicked cell.
maps.tool.pickHint: Takes the tile of the clicked cell (also: right click, or Alt+click, with any tool; right-drag copies an area of the map).
maps.fillEmptyHint: Adds woods, hills and other walkable ground to the empty space: the terrain the map has most of. Everything else stays as it is, with a free cell around it. Undo takes the filling back; another try gives another result.
maps.mouseHint: Click: paint · right click: take the tile (drag: copy an area) · Ctrl+Z: undo
maps.filterTerrain: Show only this terrain's tiles in the palette
maps.paletteHint: Duplicate tiles of the tileset are hidden. Click and drag to take several tiles.
problem.badLayout: the map is malformed (rows of different lengths)
maps.baseHint: The tile sheet gives the map its pictures and terrains (under each choice, chapters of the game using it). Changing it redraws the map cell by cell by terrain: plains stay plains, a fort stays a fort. The map plays the same; it only needs touching up. Can be undone.
maps.baseConfirm: Redraw the whole map with this tile sheet? Each cell takes a tile of the same terrain; you can undo it.
maps.baseMissing: This tile sheet does not have these terrains of the map: {terrains}. Those cells took the sheet's most common tile: touch them up.
problem.paletteNotForTileset: this palette does not go with the map's tileset
maps.changesHint: Shows the rectangles of the map changes (doors, villages, walls…)
maps.addChangeHint: New change: then draw its rectangle on the map by dragging the mouse
maps.changeEditHint: This rectangle replaces the map during play (open door, visited village...). Paint the "after" state.
maps.manualChangeHint: Paint what the map becomes once the object is used. Enlarge the rectangle for a wider passage.
problem.mapTooSmall: the map must be at least {width} × {height} cells (one screen)
problem.mapTooBig: map too big for the engine (about {cells} cells at most, and 30 × 31 in the original game)
problem.badChangeId: invalid or duplicate change number ({id}): 0 to {max}, all different
problem.changeOutOfMap: change {id} goes past the edge of the map
problem.impassableTile: unit at {x}, {y} on a terrain its class cannot go on ({terrain})
problem.weaponReserved: {item}: reserved for other classes or characters, this unit will not be able to use it
problem.weaponRank: {item}: needs rank {rank} in {wtype}, this unit will not be able to use it
problem.carriedReserved: {count} unit(s) in the chapters carry {item}, reserved for other classes or characters: they will not be able to use it
problem.carriedRank: {count} unit(s) in the chapters carry {item}, which needs rank {rank} in {wtype}: they will not be able to use it
problem.seizeOutOfMap: the tile to seize is outside the map
maps.sheetHint: The tileset as it is laid out in the game. Click and drag to take a block of tiles at once.
maps.tool.selectHint: Click a village, chest, door… to set what it gives or says.
maps.showObjectsHint: Shows the villages, houses, chests, doors, cracked walls and snags found on the map
maps.previewHint: Shows the map once every object was used: open chests, closed villages, open doors, broken walls
maps.objectsHint: Villages, chests and doors placed on the map are set up here by themselves.
maps.kindHint.village: A unit visiting it gets a gift and a message, then the village closes.
maps.kindHint.house: A unit visiting it hears a message (it can come back).
maps.kindHint.chest: Opens with a chest key, a lockpick or a thief.
maps.kindHint.door: Opens with a door key, a lockpick or a thief, and becomes floor.
maps.kindHint.wall: Can be attacked; once broken, it becomes floor. Its HP are set per chapter.
maps.kindHint.snag: Dead tree that can be attacked (20 HP); once broken, units can go through.
maps.obj.noAfter: “after” state unknown: add a change by hand
maps.obj.noChange: new · will not change its look
maps.obj.replace: Replace it with a simple message
maps.obj.textHint: Game text (no accented letters). Lines are wrapped by themselves, two per box.
maps.obj.pick: Click an object in the list (or on the map with the Objects tool) to set it.
problem.noUsedState: {object} at {x}, {y}: no known “after” state for this tileset, it will not change its look
problem.tooManyChanges: {object} at {x}, {y}: no free change number left (128 at most)
maps.transformHint: Turns or flips the chosen tile (or block). If the tileset does not have these tiles yet, FE Maker shows them and waits for your go-ahead to add them to its free slots (the maps using it see them in their palette too).
maps.similarFound: The tileset already has these tiles this way round, drawn by the game:
maps.transformError.noFreeTile: No room left for new tile pictures in this tileset.
maps.transformError.noFreeMetatile: No free slot left in this tileset.
maps.kindHint.armory: A unit on it can buy and sell weapons.
maps.kindHint.vendor: A unit on it can buy and sell items.
maps.obj.secretHint: Only a unit carrying a member card can go in.
maps.retileHint: Changes the chosen tile's terrain, on a copy: nothing else moves.
dlg.hint: Pick a message, drag portraits on the stage, click who speaks and type.
dlg.noMessage: no dialogue: ⚙ to see its commands
dlg.showStep: Show the screen at this step
dlg.textHint: Accented letters allowed (é, è, à, ç, ñ…). Lines too long are cut automatically at build time, as in the preview; an empty line = wait for a button and open a new box (two lines per box). The 😊 🤐 😑 😌 👀 😉 buttons change the expression where the cursor is.
dlg.applyLayout: Write the cuts into the text
sup.hint: Two characters who start a turn side by side gain support points: level C at {c} points, B at {b}, A at {a}. The points stop just before each level: the “Support” command then appears and the dialogue takes the pair to the level. {max} partners at most per character, and 5 levels in all.
sup.turnsHint: Turns the two must start side by side to reach each level.
problem.supportDuplicate: this pair is already in the list
problem.supportNever: with no points per turn, this support never reaches level C
problem.supportSkipsTalk: this support already starts at level {ranks}: its dialogue is never seen ({max} points at most at the start to see it)
dlg.addBattleHint: A character speaks when a fight starts (once per chapter), against someone or anyone.
dlg.addDeathHint: What a character says when defeated (in this chapter, or in all of them with “Every chapter”).
dlg.addTalkHint: A character can “Talk” to another on the map; the other one can then join the army.
dlg.addTurnHint: A dialogue at the start of a turn (player, enemy or allies), only once.
dlg.addAreaHint: A dialogue when a player unit stops in a rectangle of the map (from X1, Y1 to X2, Y2), once.
dlg.addFlagHint: A dialogue as soon as a memory (or a flag) is set by another event, once.
dlg.endTurnHint: 0: once. Otherwise the event comes back at the start of each turn, from the first to the last.
chapter.addReinforcementsHint: New group of units arriving at the start of a turn (a copy of the chapter's first enemy, to change).
chapter.newGroupHint: The units appear at the start of the chosen turn, with the game's camera on them. Place them on the map.
objective.hint.area: The chapter is won when a player unit (or the chosen character) ends its move in the area.
objective.pickingArea: Drag from one corner to the other…
objective.protectHint: The game is lost if this character dies (protection icon on the map). Works with any objective.
ev.title: Sequence of the event
ev.hint: The sequence runs top to bottom. A new action comes after the chosen step.
ev.rawHint: A game command FE Maker cannot edit yet: it is kept as it is.
ev.simple.ifTurn: If the turn is at least {n}:
ev.simple.emptyCondition: Nothing yet: choose below what should happen.
problem.noNextChapter: this ending event leads to no chapter: the game stays stuck. Add “Go to another chapter”.
problem.lostMessage: this sequence shows a dialogue that was removed
ev.op.VCWF: Change the sight in the fog
ev.tintHint: 100%: normal color; 0: black; 200: very light. Speed 0: at once. “Normal colors” ends the tint. It lasts while the event runs: the map gets its colors back afterwards, and skipping the event (Start) cancels it.
ev.counterHint: 8 counters per chapter (0 to 7), each from 0 to 15: to count visits, turns, defeated enemies…
maps.pendingTiles: This turn needs {n} new tile(s) in the tileset:
maps.pendingNudge: Create or cancel these tiles first to paint.
maps.addedTilesHint: Click a tile to take it. A tile placed on a map or in a change cannot be removed: paint over its cells first.
maps.drawNewChange: Drag on the map to draw the new change's area (Esc to cancel).
maps.drawChangeArea: Drag on the map to draw the change's new area (Esc to cancel).
maps.changeAreaHint: Draw the change's rectangle with the mouse: cells already painted keep their tiles, new ones start as the map
dlg.view.talkHint: The dialogue in bubbles: lines typed in bubbles, portraits dragged onto the stage
dlg.view.stepsHint: Every step with all its settings (off-screen positions, order of the steps)
dlg.stageHint: Drag a portrait onto the stage to place or move it, ✕ to make it leave. Click a portrait: they say the selected line, and their expressions show up.
dlg.portraitHint: {name}: click to make them speak, drag to move them
dlg.pickFaceHint: Click a portrait (it comes in at the first free place) or drag it onto the stage.
dlg.emptyMessage: Empty message: bring in a character, then type their first line below.
dlg.typeLine: Type the line… (Enter: add, Shift+Enter: new line)
flow.title: The campaign
flow.hint: Each card is a chapter; arrows show where it leads. Click one to change it.
flow.kind.title: back to the title screen
flow.otherScriptNamed: Another event of the chapter (route choice, special event…)
flow.noNext: No event of this chapter starts another chapter.
flow.goTo: Go to this chapter in the graph
flow.editHint: Changing the next chapter rewrites the event's sequence, as with the event's ⚙ button (Dialogues tab). Through the world map, its events stay the game's.
maps.tiledOpenHint: Writes the map and its changes in the project's tiled/ folder (the community's FE map layout: a "Main" layer, one layer per change with its ID property) and opens it in Tiled
maps.tiledReloadHint: Reads back the map saved in Tiled (Ctrl+S in Tiled first): the map and its changes replace FE Maker's (can be undone)
maps.tmxImportHint: A map made in Tiled or found on FE-Repo, drawn with this map's tile sheet
maps.tmxConfirm: Replace this map with "{name}" ({w} × {h})? It must be drawn with the same tile sheet. Can be undone.
maps.tiledOpened: Opened in Tiled: {path}. Save in Tiled, then "Bring back from Tiled".
maps.tiledNotInstalled: Tiled is not installed (mapeditor.org). The map is written here: {path}; open it with Tiled, save, then "Bring back from Tiled".
maps.tiledError.noTiledFile: No Tiled file for this map yet: "Open in Tiled" first.
maps.tiledError.notTmx: This file is not a Tiled map (.tmx).
maps.tiledError.unsupportedMap: Tiled map not supported: it must be orthogonal, with a fixed size.
maps.tiledError.noLayer: The Tiled map has no tile layer.
maps.tiledError.layerWithoutData: A layer of the Tiled map is empty.
maps.tiledError.unsupportedEncoding: Layer format not supported (choose CSV in the map properties, in Tiled).
maps.tiledError.unsupportedCompression: Layer compression not supported (choose CSV in the map properties, in Tiled).
maps.tiledError.badLayerSize: A layer does not have the map's size.
maps.tiledError.tileOutOfRange: The map uses tiles this tile sheet does not have: it was made with another tile sheet.
maps.tiledError.size: Size {w} × {h} not possible in the game (at least 15 × 10, at most 60 a side).
problem.missingTile: the map uses added tiles that were removed ({tiles}): the game will show garbage there. Repaint these cells or create the tiles again
dlg.exprSmileOff: Smile: off. Click to smile from the cursor on (it shows while the character talks), until the next 😊
dlg.exprSmileOn: Smile: on (until the next 😊 or the end of the message). Click to stop from the cursor on
dlg.exprMouthOff: The mouth moves while the character talks. Click to keep it still from the cursor on
dlg.exprMouthOn: Mouth still: on (until the next 🤐 or the end of the message). Click to make it move again
dlg.exprEyesNow: {what}: the eyes are like this now
dlg.exprEyesSet: {what} from the cursor on, until the eyes change again
dlg.exprWink: Wink (for a moment, where the cursor is)
maps.obj.ruin: ruins if an enemy pillages it (change {id})
problem.unknownName: "{name}" does not exist in the game (unit group, character, song or background)
ev.simpleHint: The army, the enemies, then a dialogue to write.
ev.simpleEndingHint: A dialogue to write, then the next chapter.
ev.simpleConfirm: Replace the whole event with a simple one? (can be undone)
ev.newMessageHint: New dialogue for this command (to write in the dialogue editor)
field.canSeizeHint: "Seize" command on the tile to take. In the game only Eirika and Ephraim (the route's leader) can: the Lord ability is not enough
flow.worldMapWarning: With the world map, the game picks the next chapter itself. For a new sequence, untick "World map".
flow.worldMapOn: Like the original game: the world map picks the next chapter.
flow.worldMapOff: Each chapter leads straight to the one chosen here.
flow.makeDirect: Go on without the world map
flow.noWorldMapNote: This link goes straight to the chosen chapter.
problem.manualChangeOffObject: change {id} drawn by hand for an object: it no longer holds the object's cell (snag, wall, door, chest, village), so the game will never apply it. Enlarge it to that cell
chapter.duplicateGroupHint: New reinforcements with the same units in the same places, one turn later (to change afterwards).
maps.pieceHint: {kind}, taken from: {maps}. Click, then put it on the map.
maps.pieces.buildingHint: Villages, castles, houses, forts, arenas... whole or on one tile, as the game draws them with this tile set. A click takes them as a brush.
maps.pieces.decorHint: Chests, doors, bridges, walls, pillars... A click takes them as a brush. A chest or a door you place shows in the map's objects.
chapter.prepHint: The screen where the player picks units, trades and places the army. On by default in added chapters.
chapter.wallHpHint: All the cracked walls of this chapter have these HP. Snags always have 20.
chapter.fogHint: Units only see a few cells around them (thieves and torches see farther).
banim.title: Battle animations
banim.hint: The animation as the game plays it, for each weapon of the class (arrows and thrown weapons are shown without their rotation).
banim.lib.title: Animation library (FE-Repo)
banim.lib.pick: Choose an animation to see it.
ferepo.error.rateLimited: GitHub limits requests without an account (60 an hour): try again later
banim.emptyMode: Empty movement: no weapon of the class needs it for now.
banim.import.done: "{weapon}" added to the class (⭐ in the weapon list).
banim.import.hint: The animation is downloaded, converted to the game's format and kept in the project; its authors go to the project's CREDITS.txt.
banim.import.error.noScript: this folder has no animation script (.txt)
banim.import.error.missingFrames: pictures of the script are missing from the folder
banim.import.error.badScriptLine: a line of the script is not understood
banim.import.error.frameTooBig: a picture is too big for a sheet of the game

maps.terrainEffects: Avoid +{avoid} · Def +{defense} · Res +{resistance} · Move cost: on foot {foot}, on horse {horse}
maps.colorsClick: Click the part of the map to recolour.
maps.colorsHint: Changes the colors of this palette. It is used by {n} chapter(s): all of them change. The fog color follows by itself.
maps.sizeHint: Cells to add on each side (a negative number removes some); new cells get the selected tile.
maps.moveConfirm: Warning: coordinates written in events do not follow. An event may aim at the wrong cells, or freeze the game. Changes, villages, chests, doors, units and seize tiles follow the map. Continue?
banim.rangedHint: The ranged attack of the sword, lance or axe casts a spell: what a magic weapon needs. The gesture varies between animations: check the "Ranged attack" movement once imported.
banim.weaponFilterHint: Looking up each animation's weapons: the first time, FE Maker asks GitHub (a few seconds, up to a minute for "All folders"), then it is kept for a week. When several are ticked, the animation must have them all.
banim.missingFolders: {n} folder(s) not checked yet: GitHub allows 60 requests an hour. Their animations are missing from the list; try again later.
banim.local.title: From my PC
banim.local.hint: Choose a weapon's folder (the FEditor .txt script and its frames, as on FE-Repo) or its .zip. Remember to write its authors in the project's CREDITS.txt.
banim.local.name: Animation name
character.addAllyHint: Add a playable character (16 free places in the game)
character.addEnemyHint: Add an enemy or a non-playable character: boss, NPC…
character.noFree: No free place left in the game's character table for this kind.
character.removeConfirm: Remove {name}? The chapters and dialogues using them will be flagged.
problem.characterEntryTaken: this character's place in the game's table is used by the game: remove it and create it again
item.newFrom: New item based on this one
item.newFromHint: Adds an item to the game, a copy of this one: same effect (healing, key, staff…), same spell and battle animations; name, stats, uses, price and icon to adjust afterwards (49 places after the game's items)
item.actsLikeHint: The game's item whose in-game effect this one has (healing, key, staff, potion…): by default the one it copies. Name, stats, range and uses stay its own.
item.tempBonusesHint: What the item gives when drunk, stat by stat, from -8 (malus) to +7; each bonus or malus moves 1 point toward 0 each turn. Drinking again sets the item's values back.
item.amountHealHint: The HP this item gives back. A staff adds its user's Magic (80 at most).
item.noFree: No free place left after the game's items.
item.effectHint: Poison: poisons the target. Nosferatu: drains HP. Eclipse: halves the target's HP. Devil: may hurt its user. Stone: petrifies the target.
item.weaponExpHint: Weapon rank points won with each use: 1 for most weapons.
item.bonusesHint: A weapon gives them while equipped, a consumable gives them for good. Move and constitution: consumables only.
item.prop.magicHint: Targets resistance and counts all of the Force. Blocked by Silence, it loses a use even when it misses.
item.prop.magicSwordHint: The setting of Light Brand, Wind Sword and Runesword: targets resistance, no rank points. These three swords also have their own formula, tied to their number.
item.prop.uncounterableHint: Neither unit counterattacks in this battle.
item.prop.negateDefenseHint: The target's defense or resistance does not count.
item.prop.noRepairHint: The Hammerne staff cannot repair it.
item.prop.negateFlyingHint: A unit carrying it no longer takes effective damage against fliers.
item.prop.negateCritHint: A unit carrying it no longer takes critical hits.
item.spellHint: The effect the weapon casts, taken from another weapon: it shows if the unit's animation casts a spell or a projectile.
item.noSpell: Pick a spell in Properties: without one, nothing fires at range.
item.noRangedAnimation: No "Ranged attack" movement in the animation of these classes:
item.noRangedHow: Import an animation for each ("Strikes at range" filter of the library), or keep the weapon up close.
problem.noRangedAnimation: No "Ranged attack" movement in the animation of {classes}: import one ("Strikes at range" filter of the library), or keep the weapon up close.
item.removeConfirm: Remove {name}? The units, chests and shops having it will be flagged.
problem.itemNumberTaken: this item number is used by the game: remove the weapon and create it again
problem.unknownModel: the weapon this one copies does not exist
class.newFrom: New class based on this one
class.newFromHint: Adds a class to the game, a copy of this one: same sprites, battle animations and promotions, to adjust afterwards
class.noFree: No free place left after the game's classes.
class.removeConfirm: Remove {name}? The characters and units having it will be flagged.

ev.op.BGE: If greater or equal, go to
ev.op.BLE: If less or equal, go to

ev.memory.name: Memory
ev.if.memory: If the player has this memory…
ev.if.notMemory: If the player does not have this memory…
ev.if.turn: If the turn is at least…
mapsprite.title: Sprite on the map
mapsprite.error.notAnImage: this file is not a picture
mapsprite.error.badStandSize: the standing sprite must be 16 × 48, 16 × 96 or 32 × 96
options.defaultsHint: What the player finds when starting a game; they can change it in game.
options.tempBonusRuleHint: When a unit drinks a Pure Water copy while it already has a temporary bonus or malus on the same stat.
options.tempBonusRule.strongest: The strongest wins (a bonus and a malus add up)
options.skipOpeningHint: The game starts on the save menu.
options.skipStoryIntroHint: Removes the tale of Magvel shown when a new game starts.
options.talkBubblesHint: A yellow bubble on the units the selected one can talk to, or has a support ready with.
options.quickChapterTitleHint: The title can be skipped at once.
options.holdAToSpeedUp: Hold A to speed up movement
options.stationaryRange: No range for units that never move
options.stationaryRangeHint: An enemy that stays shows only what it can strike.
options.statusGrowthsHint: On the first page of a unit's status screen, Select shows its growth rates in place of its stats; the name of each stat of player units takes the colour of its growth, from red (low) to green (high).
options.battleNumbersHint: In battle animations, lost HP show in red above the unit hit, restored HP in green (staff healing, drain).
flow.add.button: Add a chapter after this one
flow.add.title: Title
flow.add.hint: Takes a free slot of the game: empty map, no enemies. Slots left: {n}.
flow.add.noFreeChapter: no free slot left for a chapter
flow.add.badMapSize: the map must be from 15 × 10 to 64 × 64
flow.music.title: Player phase music
flow.music.hint: The MIDI plays with the game's instruments: the sound depends on the file.
flow.music.notAMidi: this file is not a MIDI
problem.titleTooLong: the title does not fit in the chapter's title picture: shorten it
options.editorHint: FE Maker's settings for this project: they do not change the game.
portrait.none: This character has no portrait yet.
portrait.newHintNone: A 128 × 112 sheet, from your PC or FE-Repo.
banim.reopenHint: Open it again in the library below
ws.backHint: Back to the previous screen (Alt + left arrow)
options.showOriginal: Show the ways back to the original game
options.showOriginalHint: Useful if you edit the existing game. If you start from scratch, untick it: the "back to the original" buttons go away, your changes stay.
home.blankHint: A single empty chapter, then you choose what you keep of the game.
project.tooNew: This project comes from a newer version of FE Maker: update FE Maker to open it. The project was not changed.
project.migrationFailed: This project could not be converted for this version: it was put back as it was, and a copy is in its backups folder.
flow.endGameHint: The end of this chapter goes back to the title screen
checks.title: To install before you start
checks.decomp.missing: FE Maker downloads it from GitHub, once (a few minutes). It contains no ROM data.
checks.docker.missing: It compiles the game. Install Docker Desktop, free for personal use.
checks.docker.stopped: Docker is installed but does not answer: start Docker Desktop and wait until it is ready. If it never starts, virtualization (Intel VT-x, AMD-V) is probably off in the BIOS.
checks.docker.starting: FE Maker is starting Docker Desktop: allow about a minute. If it never starts, virtualization (Intel VT-x, AMD-V) is probably turned off in the BIOS.
checks.toolchain.missing: They build the game, with nothing else to install. FE Maker downloads them from GitHub, once (about 25 MB).
checks.firstBuild.running: FE Maker is preparing the game's build, once (about ten minutes). You can already work: your tests will then be quick.
checks.firstBuild.failed: The first build failed. It will start again at the next launch; if it keeps failing, send a ticket.
checks.mgba.missing: This emulator runs the tests. Without it you can still export a patch.
checks.error.unreachable: GitHub does not answer: check your connection, then try again.
checks.error.badArchive: The download is incomplete: try again.
ticket.issueHint: Opens a filled-in report in your browser: you read it before sending it
ticket.issueImages: ({n} screenshot(s) to drag here by hand)
options.quickLevelUpHint: The window stays for less time.
options.noSupportAnimations: "Staff & Dance" line in the game's menu
options.noSupportAnimationsHint: The player chooses whether staves and dances use the battle screen.
field.descriptionLong: The game shows two lines of about {n} characters: this text may overflow.
options.casualModeHint: A fallen unit comes back for the next chapter.
options.strMagSplitHint: Magic becomes its own stat: it counts for tomes, magic swords at range and staves, strength for the rest.
options.skillsHint: Characters and classes get skills (3 at most each), shown with their icon on the unit's status screen; R shows their effect. The game's class abilities are listed there too.
skill.title: Skills
skill.hint: {n} at most per sheet. A unit has its character's and its class's; its status screen in the game shows 6.
skill.learnedHint: {n} at most. The character learns the skill on reaching this level; it keeps 4 at most (the oldest is forgotten for a 5th). Player only.
skill.learnedClassHint: {n} at most. A unit of this class learns the skill on reaching this level; level 1: on being promoted into this class. It keeps 4 at most. Player only.
skill.DefiantStrHint: Strength +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantMagHint: Magic +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantSklHint: Skill +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantSpdHint: Speed +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantLckHint: Luck +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantDefHint: Defense +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantResHint: Resistance +7 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantCritHint: Crit rate +50 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.DefiantAvoidHint: Avoid +30 while under a quarter of max HP.
skill.BlowDartingHint: Speed +6 in a battle the unit starts.
skill.BlowDeathHint: Attack +6 in a battle the unit starts, with a physical weapon.
skill.BlowArmoredHint: Defense +6 in a battle the unit starts, against a physical attack.
skill.BlowWardingHint: Resistance +6 in a battle the unit starts, against a magic attack.
skill.WrathHint: Crit rate +20 while under half of max HP.
skill.VantageHint: Attacked while under half of max HP, the unit strikes first.
skill.DesperationHint: When the unit attacks while under half of max HP, its second attack comes right after the first, before the counter.
skill.LunaHint: Ignores the enemy's defense (physical attack). Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.CoronaHint: Ignores the enemy's resistance (magic attack). Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.SolHint: Restores the damage dealt as HP. Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.AetherHint: Ignores 80% of the enemy's defense and restores the damage dealt as HP. Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.IgnisHint: Adds half the defense (the resistance with magic) to the attack. Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.ColossusHint: Triples the damage, shown as a critical hit. Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.PaviseHint: Nullifies a physical attack, as Great Shield does. Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.AegisHint: Nullifies a magic attack, as Great Shield does. Activation chance: the unit's Skill, in %.
skill.AdeptHint: One more hit in each attack while the unit has full HP.
skill.AstraHint: When the unit starts the battle: 5 hits instead of one, damage halved. Activation chance: the unit's Speed, in %. A battle keeps 6 hits at most, as in the game.
skill.CantoHint: Can move again after acting (Canto ability).
skill.LockTouchHint: Opens doors and chests without keys (Thief skills ability).
skill.DanceHint: Can dance or play to let a unit act again (Dance and Play abilities).
skill.SupplyHint: Opens the convoy (Supply ability, or the route's lord: Eirika or Ephraim).
skill.LethalityHint: May kill in one hit; chance of half the skill (Lethality ability).
skill.SummonHint: Can call a phantom that fights (Summon ability).
skill.SureShotHint: Sure hit, damage +50%; chance equal to the level (Sniper).
skill.PierceHint: Ignores the enemy's defense; chance equal to the level (Wyvern Knight).
skill.GreatShieldHint: Nullifies an attack; chance equal to the level (General).
options.actAfterTalkHint: Talking or using a support no longer ends the unit's turn: it can still attack, trade or wait. As in recent Fire Emblem games.
options.dangerZoneHint: Select shows the tiles enemies can strike; Select or B to go back.
chapter.weatherHint: What the map shows during the chapter. Rain, snow and sandstorms slow some classes down (their movement costs by weather).
chapter.battleBgHint: The scenery behind the fighters depends on the cell they fight on; this setting picks the set of sceneries (castle, ruins, desert...). In brackets: the game's chapters using it.
chapter.cameraHint: The cell the camera shows during the chapter's title, before the first event.
item.iconHint: A 16 x 16 icon, brought to the colors shared by the game's icons. The game only leaves 11 free places.
ferepo.notIcon: This file is not 16 x 16 pixels.
ferepo.error.badIconSize: an icon must be 16 x 16 pixels
ferepo.error.noFreeIcon: no free place left for an icon
chapter.statsHint: Character sheet and class, as in the game in normal mode. Automatic levels are random: this is their average, the result varies a little in each playthrough.
chapter.ranksHint: Weapon ranks: the character sheet's, else the class's.
chapter.ranksAutoHint: Weapon ranks: the character sheet's, else the class's. With autolevel, the game raises each type's rank to what the most demanding weapon or staff in the inventory needs, if the unit already has a rank in that type. The level does not matter.
chapter.turnFocusHint: Show on the map the units there at this turn (the ones that came before greyed out). Click again to see everything.
chapter.timelineHint: One row per turn where units come. Click a turn to show it on the map; “Duplicate this group”, in an open group, copies it one turn later.
chapter.addSceneGroupHint: A group of units that an event brings (cutscene), never on its own in battle.
chapter.notBrought: No event brings this group yet.
chapter.sceneGroupHint: Place its units on the map, then, in an event's sequence (Dialogues tab), add “Load a unit group” and pick this group. Units come in from their starting position and go to their arrival position; “Remove a unit” takes them away.
dlg.sequenceHint: The event's commands: its dialogue, and whatever you want before or after it (bring units, tint the screen, weather, HP, sound…).
dlg.areaDraw: Draw the area on the map by dragging from one corner to the other.
chapter.itemDrop: Drops their last item on death
chapter.itemDropHint: If the player defeats them, the unit landing the blow gets the last item of their inventory. In game, this item is green on their sheet.
ws.changesHint: The latest changes of all tabs
ws.changesBack: Go back to before this change
scope.title: What this project keeps
scope.hint: What is unticked leaves the project's lists; chapters become free slots. The data is copied first.
scope.chaptersHint: A removed chapter only comes back with the data copy.
scope.charactersHint: Their places serve "+ Ally" and "+ Enemy". The hero stays.
scope.classesHint: Those of kept characters and chapters stay.
scope.confirm: Apply these choices to the project? Its data is copied first.
scope.done: Done. Data copied to {path}. {n} element(s) kept because a kept chapter needs them.
scope.needed: A kept chapter uses it: it stays
ev.simple.hint: The event step by step. Click a step to change it.
ev.simple.dropEnd: Drop here to put it at the end
ev.simple.empty: This event has no visible step: add one, or switch to the detailed view.
flow.renameHint: Empty: the original title comes back. The title picture follows at the next build.
problem.chapterNoEnemies: "{title}" has no enemies: it ends on the first turn
problem.chapterNoNext: "{title}" leads nowhere: link it or end the game here
maps.groundHint: Paint a river, a road, a cliff: the tiles join by themselves, as on the game's maps. Painting plains erases cleanly.
